headline: 902 traffic injuries last year is the most in Chicago, even as Ward 28 leads on gardens.
summary:
Ward 28 stretches across Near West Side, East Garfield Park, West Garfield Park, and Austin, with a composite score of 36.54 that puts it 36th out of 50, below the citywide midpoint. The ward has more mapped gardens than anywhere else in the city, 23 in total, and ranks fourth on the count of civic, cultural, and public places, with 136 mapped. It also ranks fourth on the share of aldermanic menu money spent resurfacing alleys, at 44.7 percent, and fourth on new residential permits issued, 29 in total. Modeled estimates put the ward third in the city on how often residents socialize with neighbors weekly, 18.3 percent, and fourth on seeing friends weekly, 20.7 percent, though both figures come from a statistical model rather than a survey of the ward itself.

The weak spots cluster around safety and cost of living. Ward 28 recorded 902 traffic injuries last year, the highest count of the fifty. Close to half of its licensed restaurants, 49.2 percent, are chain outlets rather than independents, near the foot of that ranking citywide. Almost a third of residents, 30.5 percent, live below the poverty line, 48th of 50, and the ward also posts weak numbers on faith diversity among houses of worship and on two separate readings of pollution exposure, both tied to Superfund and brownfield sites and other contaminated land nearby.
reading_the_rankings: The third and fourth-place ranks on how often residents see friends and neighbors weekly, 18.3 percent and 20.7 percent, read like real community strength, but neither number is measured inside Ward 28 at all. Both come out of a model built on age, income, and household make-up in wards with similar demographics and density, not anything counted on these blocks, and whoever built the estimate calls it low confidence too. The 50th-place rank on traffic injuries, 902 people hurt in police-reported crashes last year, is a more literal count, though that category's field comes up short of the full fifty, since not every ward logs enough crash data to be compared. The poverty rate, 48th of 50 at 30.5 percent, is an area-weighted number. It comes from splitting each census tract by how much of its area sits inside the ward line, then counting the tract's population toward whichever ward holds the bigger slice. Wherever a tract straddles the boundary, some of that 30.5 percent really belongs next door.

news.headline: Rev. Don Hoover Wheat Remembered As Champion Of Civil Rights On The West Side
news.note: Neighbors remembered Rev. Don Hoover Wheat, who led Third Unitarian Church in Austin from 1969 to 1998, after his death at age 92.

news.headline: 3 Families Prepare To Move Into Habitat For Humanity's 1st West Side Homes
news.note: Habitat for Humanity is finishing its first three homes in Austin, part of a larger push to build affordable housing on the West Side.

news.headline: 7 Save A Lot Stores on South, West Sides Could Close In Days As Owners Face 'Financial Headwinds'
news.note: The West Garfield Park Save A Lot at 420 South Pulaski Road was among seven citywide locations facing sudden closure while city officials worked with the owners to try to keep them open.

news.headline: Florals By Hailey: West Side Art Teacher Launching Floral Studio In Austin Arts District With Workshops For Neighbors
news.note: Nash Elementary art teacher Hailey Rodden is opening a floral studio and workshop space on West North Avenue in Austin's developing arts district.
